blockingFindings.title: Late assertion evidence can crash result construction
blockingFindings.issue: `childProcessResult()` determines `kind` using `utf8Prefix(stdoutText/stderrText, captureLimitBytes)`, but `ChildProcessExecutionResult` later constructs `ProcessStreamCapture` with `boundedDiagnosticContent()`, which intentionally relocates late assertion evidence into the captured stream. When assertion evidence appears after the initial byte prefix, the kind is set to `nonzero-exit`, then the constructor invariant rejects the captured assertion evidence and throws instead of returning an `assertion-failure` record.
blockingFindings.suggestion: In `childProcessResult()`, classify assertion evidence from the same bounded stream content used by `ProcessStreamCapture`, or construct the stream captures before choosing `kind` and pass their `.content` values into `hasAssertionEvidence()`.
blockingFindings.rationale: R2 requires numeric exits to use `assertion-failure` when assertion evidence is present while keeping plain numeric exits distinct. The current implementation fails that mandatory behavior for bounded output where assertion evidence is outside the simple prefix, and can throw before producing the required typed child diagnostic record.
